A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LightRetriever work. All 28 pages of v2 and 29 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval experiments, query-encoding measurements, ablations, and index-size analyses, with detailed benchmark results in the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains original retrieval results and reports additional end-to-end timing, hybrid-baseline comparisons, and a query-encoder ablation.

M1.justification: The full document encoder, cached and averaged dense query-token embeddings, sparse token counts, and training losses remain. The auxiliary KL loss moves to Appendix A.4. V3 specifies normalized-score summation within the earlier linear-fusion description; the PDFs do not establish a changed procedure. The one-layer encoder is an ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 23 training datasets, 15 English BeIR tasks, eight Chinese CMTEB retrieval tasks, and MS MARCO web-search data. V3's expanded dataset list restates appendix coverage. Timing full retrieval over a specified passage subset changes evaluation procedure, without establishing a new task or domain.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds evaluated Static Embedding + BM25 and BGE-m3 dense+sparse hybrid comparators. The symmetric baseline row in v2's KL comparison, Table 3, is omitted from v3 Table 5. Existing pretrained comparators and the appendix Mistral comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 Table 1 measures Mistral query encoding on H800 across batch sizes 16–8192, including CPU encoding. V3 replaces this with Llama/Qwen retrieval on A800 at batch size 256 over one million passages, adding search time, total time, and QPS. It specifies 1k-dimensional Faiss exact search and 64-thread Lucene search. This substantially changes the efficiency protocol; retained accuracy results do not establish rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds the first-Transformer-layer query ablation in Section 4, A3, while removing instruction-removal and binary sparse-weight tests and the batch-size timing sweep. Reverse-asymmetry results survive only qualitatively. Most central analyses remain: vector-size and KL studies move to Appendices A.3–A.4, and Figure 5 redisplays existing dense/sparse/hybrid results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table superscripts indicate performance differences, and the figures provide no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 replaces the timing results, reporting 6,999/6,982 QPS for LightRetriever versus 549/592 for corresponding full LLMs under its new settings. Tables 2 and 4 add hybrid-baseline and first-layer results. LightRetriever dense/sparse recall entries, Mistral recall entries, and several ablation entries disappear, while appendix per-dataset nDCG scores remain identical. V3's Llama-best BeIR statement conflicts with higher E5-Mistral and retained appendix Mistral scores.

T1.justification: The retrieval objective, representation definitions, losses, attention-mask definition, and sparse-aggregation derivation and Algorithm 1 are mathematically unchanged. Relocating KL alignment and renumbering equations introduce no new theory or proof.

C1.justification: The lightweight-query architecture, over-1000× encoding speedup, and approximately 95% performance-retention claims remain. V3's abstract and introduction add over-10× end-to-end retrieval throughput and shift the hardware comparison to A800. The conclusion still retains v2's H800 and CPU-speedup claims.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the timing breakdown as identifying query encoding as the main bottleneck and explains why retaining one Transformer layer conflicts with its inference-efficiency goal. It removes v2's interpretation that co-occurrence matters more than sparse term frequency and its Chinese-pretraining explanation for Qwen's advantage. Appendix A.1's applicability limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds search implementation settings and explicitly describes normalized-score summation. Training hardware is reported as eight H800 or A800 GPUs, replacing the H800-only description; CPU/RAM specifications and the direct tDRO training-data link disappear. The code-release promise, dataset sampling and decontamination details, task instructions, and optimization algorithm remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix A.2 remain unchanged, including the existing novelty claim about LLM query efficiency. V3 modestly expands main-text positioning against efficient Static Embedding + BM25 and strong BGE-m3 hybrid retrieval, and explains SPLADE's exclusion from the bilingual comparison.

P1.justification: The experimental settings, results discussion, and ablation narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Section 4 becomes a sequence of A1–A4 questions, while KL-method discussion and two former main-text experimental subsections move into the appendix. Architecture captions receive substantial explanatory expansion.

P2.justification: V3 substantially restructures the efficiency, accuracy, and ablation tables; adds an architecture-configuration table; and introduces a bar-chart redisplay of existing component scores. The vector-size figure and KL table move into the appendix. These changes materially alter how the main evidence is displayed, beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the practical efficiency evidence by extending v2's encoding-only measurements to end-to-end retrieval throughput, while new hybrid comparators improve the relevance of accuracy comparisons. These gains are partly offset by lost diagnostic results and discussion inconsistencies: the BeIR ranking overlooks higher Mistral scores, and the unchanged H800/CPU conclusion loses its supporting timing table. With the method and most accuracy evidence unchanged, the net quality improvement is limited.
